223: She had heard it first in the kitchen, lost it in the hall, and found it again here, through her hand as much as her ears. A low continuous hum, below the refrigerator’s register. The refrigerator cycled. This did not. In the whole slow hour she spent at that end of the house it never once rested, never changed pitch, never acknowledged the compressor’s duty to stop. She checked the panel: nothing tripped, nothing labeled in a way that answered the question. She wrote, continuous hum, garage side, source not identified, and the sentence looked wrong in her field notes, the way an unpaid balance looks wrong in a ledger, and she left it there because it was true.
225: The floor plan had come with the commission packet, a photocopy of the county’s drawing of the house, made for tax purposes by someone who had never needed the house to be anything but taxable. The plan showed eleven interior doors. She counted doors as she walked, because doors are openings and openings are inventory, and she arrived at the end of the hall with twelve.
226: She stood still and ran the count again from memory. Then she ran it a third time on her feet, room by room, touching each jamb with two fingers as she passed, the way a teller counts other people’s money. Eleven.
227: She wrote both numbers in the field notes, the twelve struck through once, the eleven set beside it, and the strike-through annoyed her more than the discrepancy. Counting was the thing she did not get wrong. She added the likeliest cause for the record, a pair of bifold closet doors countable as one or as two depending on the walker’s mood, and initialed the correction. The note was for a future reader who would never ask. The note was for her.
228: [E.] The plan referenced is the Travis County appraisal district drawing of the property, last revised August 2019, reproduced in this volume as Plate XI. It shows 11 interior doors. The Editor has not counted them.
797: White light contains all frequencies. A prism separates what is already present. The temporal prism does not add knowledge the model lacks; it selects which knowledge dominates. The model had read everything, every Lincoln at once, the way white light is every color at once. You could not take knowledge out of it. But you could govern which knowledge arrived dominant, by seeding the context, by giving the summons a lens. Nothing added. Nothing invented. Selection, which is what a prism does, and what an archive does, and what, Hale would append in one letter that summer, a historian is.
798: The folder records one call between them that spring, on the tenth of March, ninety minutes by video, and the call left one sentence behind on the whiteboard in Thorne’s marker, under the triangle, where the photograph keeps it: We are not bringing historians into AI architecture. We are bringing language models into the archive. Miranda read it twice and did not write it down. She did not need to. She was standing in the archive.
799: Three rooms, then. Three lenses on one man.
800: Condition I, the contemporary lens: the summons seeded with a single modern life of the subject, Meacham’s And There Was Light, 2022, the whole arc of the man refracted through one present-day sensibility, sympathetic, literary, complete. Condition II, the primary source lens: the summons seeded with nothing but the man’s own hand, letters, speeches, fragments, resolutions, chosen and bounded by a historian. And Condition III, the control: the summons seeded with nothing at all. The bare model. The protocol files and an empty folder where the matter should be. On the whiteboard, in the photograph, the third room’s seed is a single word in brackets, and Thorne had written that one word in red marker: the room left bare on purpose, to see what walks in when nothing is invited.
